graph.title: Row-column Scanning to control an 8x8 LED Matrix
notes: Fixed the V4 errors. Each breadboard rail hole takes one lead, and the Uno 5V and GND wires had shared rail holes with the pot supply wires. Each wire now has its own hole: 5V goes to tp.1, pot 1 supply to tp.2 and pot 2 supply to tp.3. GND goes to tn.1, pot 1 ground to tn.2 and pot 2 ground to tn.3. All tp holes are one strip and all tn holes are one strip, so the electrical result is the same.
Parts are unchanged from step 1: 1 Uno, 1 8x8 matrix, 1 breadboard, 2 pots, 8 1k resistors, 24 jumper wires.

Matrix wiring follows the tutorial's pin table. Arduino pins map to matrix rows and columns as: 13=R5, 12=R7, 11=C2, 10=C3, A2(16)=R8, A3(17)=C5, A4(18)=R6, A5(19)=R3, 2=R1, 3=C4, 4=C6, 5=R4, 6=C1, 7=R2, 8=C7, 9=C8.

The tutorial doesn't say which side the 8 resistors go on. I put all 8 on the column (cathode) wires, which are the yellow wires 1-8. Each resistor's other leg plugs into the Uno header. The row wires 9-16 are green and have no resistor.

The image doesn't show which breadboard holes are used. I assumed pot1 sits in 5t.a, 6t.a and 7t.a (GND, SIG, VCC) and pot2 in 12t.a, 13t.a and 14t.a. Pot 1's wiper goes to A0 and pot 2's wiper to A1.

graph_initial.title: Row-column Scanning to control an 8x8 LED Matrix
notes: Step 1 parts are unchanged: 1 Uno, 1 8x8 matrix, 1 breadboard, 2 pots, 8 1k resistors, 24 jumper wires.

Matrix wiring follows the tutorial's pin table. Arduino pins map to matrix rows and columns as: 13=R5, 12=R7, 11=C2, 10=C3, A2(16)=R8, A3(17)=C5, A4(18)=R6, A5(19)=R3, 2=R1, 3=C4, 4=C6, 5=R4, 6=C1, 7=R2, 8=C7, 9=C8. This matches the catalogue's matrix pin numbering (rows R1-R8 = pins 9,14,8,12,1,7,2,5; columns C1-C8 = pins 13,3,4,10,6,11,15,16).

The tutorial says the 8 resistors go on the yellow wires but doesn't say which side. I put all 8 on the column (cathode) wires, following the rule that resistors go on the same side. These are the yellow wires 1-8, each running from a resistor to a matrix column. The resistor's other leg plugs straight into the Uno header. The row wires 9-16 are green and have no resistor.

The image doesn't show which breadboard holes are used. I assumed pot1 sits in 5t.a, 6t.a and 7t.a (GND, SIG, VCC) and pot2 in 12t.a, 13t.a and 14t.a. The Uno 5V goes to the tp rail and GND.1 to the tn rail, and short wires link each pot's outer legs to the rails.
Pot 1's wiper goes to A0 and pot 2's wiper to A1, as the tutorial's circuit text says.
